title: Multi-branch preprocessing hypotheses for blind SCOBY material identity and process-history gating
scope: Comparative hypothesis registry for multiple SCOBY preprocessing branches before any subsequent thermal or microwave treatment. This record does not authorize or provide an experimental recipe for microwave treatment of flammable solvents, glycerol-containing samples, or other hazardous mixtures.
branch_comparison_principle: Each preprocessing branch is a competing process-history hypothesis. No branch receives a preferred material class or application class before matched controls, blind identity, and characterization.

qualitative_hypotheses: Changing liquid composition may alter microwave coupling and spatial/temporal heating history.
Earlier solvent evaporation may alter vapor-generation and mechanical-stress history.
Local vapor accumulation may change oxygen availability, but does not establish an inert or reducing atmosphere.
Final mass yield, porosity, surface chemistry, and electrical properties may differ from a water-rich matched control.
A_ETHANOL_SOLVENT_EXCHANGE.claim_boundary: Do not infer higher carbon yield, nanopore preservation, graphitization, or reducing-atmosphere behavior without direct measurements and matched controls.

qualitative_hypotheses: Lower water content should change dielectric coupling relative to wet SCOBY, but the magnitude must be measured rather than inferred from dryness alone.
Residual bound water, salts, or mineral components could produce spatially heterogeneous heating.
Reduced free-water evaporation may change mechanical disruption and thermal decomposition history.
Drying may produce shrinkage and densification before any subsequent treatment.
B_AIR_DRY_NO_TENSION.claim_boundary: Low moisture does not by itself establish weak microwave heating, absence of hot spots, preservation of geometry, or low surface area.

qualitative_hypotheses: Macroscopic tension may alter shrinkage and in-plane fiber orientation during drying.
Anisotropic precursor morphology may alter later dimensional change or electrical anisotropy if a conductive phase forms.
Differential stress release may produce curling, delamination, cracking, or warping.
Any claim of fiber-orientation retention requires direct structural evidence.
C_AIR_DRY_UNDER_TENSION.claim_boundary: An oriented precursor is not evidence of carbon-fiber-like or graphitic material; orientation must be demonstrated experimentally.

qualitative_hypotheses: Glycerol retention can alter plasticization, residual liquid content, drying shrinkage, and thermal history.
A glycerol-containing matrix may exhibit substantially different heating behavior from water-only or dry controls.
Thermal decomposition of glycerol-containing material may generate a chemically different residue and gas/vapor profile.
A foamed or highly porous residue is possible but cannot be inferred from glycerol presence alone.
D_GLYCEROL_DURING_DRYING.claim_boundary: Do not infer superior microwave absorption, foaming, acrolein formation, carbon yield, or macroporosity without controlled measurements. Thermal decomposition products must be treated as potentially hazardous.

qualitative_hypotheses: Replacing part of the aqueous phase with glycerol may alter dielectric heating and evaporation behavior.
Residual water and glycerol together may generate a different thermal history from either water-rich or dry controls.
Glycerol decomposition may change residue chemistry, but any contribution of glycerol-derived carbon must be demonstrated rather than inferred.
The resulting material may be chemically heterogeneous or mixed-phase.
E_GLYCEROL_SOLVENT_EXCHANGE.claim_boundary: Do not infer that glycerol automatically acts as a reducing medium, preserves pores, produces a carbon foam, or increases carbon yield.

minimum_comparators.A_ETHANOL_SOLVENT_EXCHANGE: matched_water-rich control from same precursor batch
minimum_comparators.B_AIR_DRY_NO_TENSION: matched drying-only control with recorded moisture endpoint
minimum_comparators.C_AIR_DRY_UNDER_TENSION: B_AIR_DRY_NO_TENSION with matched drying endpoint and tension as the principal process-history difference
minimum_comparators.D_GLYCEROL_DURING_DRYING: matched drying branch without glycerol from same precursor batch
minimum_comparators.E_GLYCEROL_SOLVENT_EXCHANGE: matched water-rich branch and matched glycerol-free exchange/control

matched_control_matrix.interpretation_rule: No downstream effect may be attributed to a preprocessing branch unless the design isolates preprocessing history from precursor, mass, geometry, liquid content, atmosphere, and subsequent treatment history.

blind_identity_gate_extensions.prohibited_inference: Color, brittleness, low density, apparent foaming, preserved shape, or visual porosity cannot independently establish material identity.

process_history_extension.subsequent_treatment_rule: Any microwave or thermal treatment must be represented as a separate process event with complete thermal, microwave, atmosphere, and safety metadata inherited from v2.6/v2.7.

A_ETHANOL_SOLVENT_EXCHANGE.heating_hypothesis: changed dielectric coupling and evaporation history

B_AIR_DRY_NO_TENSION.heating_hypothesis: weaker bulk coupling with possible localized hot spots

C_AIR_DRY_UNDER_TENSION.heating_hypothesis: similar bulk regime to dry control but altered morphology/history

D_GLYCEROL_DURING_DRYING.heating_hypothesis: potentially altered heating due to retained glycerol
D_GLYCEROL_DURING_DRYING.mechanical_hypothesis: plasticization may reduce shrinkage before treatment

application_gate.rule: No branch is assigned a supercapacitor, artistic-carbon, biochar, soil-amendment, cosmetic, biomedical, food, or other application class from preprocessing hypotheses alone.

safety_boundary.flammable_solvent_microwave: Ethanol and other flammable solvents may generate flammable vapors and serious ignition/fire/pressure hazards under microwave heating. This registry does not authorize or provide instructions for such treatment.
safety_boundary.glycerol_containing_microwave: Glycerol-containing biological material can undergo uncontrolled heating and thermal decomposition and may generate hazardous vapors or ignite. This registry does not authorize or provide instructions for such treatment.
safety_boundary.dry_biopolymer_microwave: Dry biological polymers can develop localized hot spots, smoke, charring, arcing, or ignition. Household microwave treatment is not an approved experimental platform.
safety_boundary.tensioned_samples: Fixtures must not introduce conductive or arcing components into microwave environments; registry metadata records geometry and fixture history but does not constitute apparatus instructions.
safety_boundary.vapors: Unknown thermal-decomposition vapors require appropriate laboratory engineering controls and analytical handling.
safety_boundary.powders: Unknown carbonaceous residues and fine particulates require appropriate containment and inhalation controls.
safety_boundary.food_boundary: No branch is a food, beverage, cosmetic, medical, or human-consumption pathway.

next_gate: REGISTER_A_BLIND_MULTIBRANCH_DATASET_WITH_MATCHED_CONTROLS; RECORD_COMPLETE_PREPROCESSING_AND_SUBSEQUENT_TREATMENT HISTORY; PERFORM IDENTITY AND STRUCTURE CHARACTERIZATION WITHOUT APPLICATION EXPECTATION; ONLY THEN OPEN FUNCTIONAL TESTING.
authority_rule: This record extends v2.7 by adding competing preprocessing branches and matched-control requirements. It does not convert any qualitative branch hypothesis into a validated material class, synthesis protocol, safety approval, or application claim.
